transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07 14:30 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Vertex Head of ML), Tom Madsen (Vertex Platform), Lina Duarte (Product), Evan Park (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick handshake to lock acceptance gates and reporting format, understand traffic profile and what tests to run.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for making time, quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Singh: Priya here, hi Maya, hi Carlos.
[00:08] Tom Madsen: Tom - platform.
[00:10] Lina Duarte: Lina from product.
[00:12] Carlos Rivera: Carlos here - will own the bench runs and configs.
[00:15] Evan Park: Evan - SRE, here for the networking bits.
[00:20] Maya Chen: cool, objective for today is to agree on the go/no-go thresholds and the exact acceptance test artifacts so when we run the bench next week we have a crystal clear pass/fail. Does that align?
[00:30] Priya Singh: yep, that's exactly it. We're particularly nervous about tail latency under peak and model accuracy for intent classification.
[00:36] Carlos Rivera: makes sense, so we've sketched a playbook: three main runs - baseline (fp16), quantized (int8-ish), and caching enabled. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 generation latency, tokens/sec, and correctness metrics against your labelled set.
[00:48] Lina Duarte: how do you define correctness here? Is it exact string match or semantic accuracy?
[00:52] Maya Chen: good q — for routing use-case Priya described, we'll use intent accuracy over your labelled intents with thresholds you set; also a secondary QA metric where we do top-1 semantic similarity for replies.
[01:02] Priya Singh: our initial thought: intent accuracy >= 92% and semantic similarity (embedding cosine) > 0.86 for accepted responses. Anything below that triggers manual review.
[01:12] Carlos Rivera: ok noted, we'll surface both. For latency, what's acceptable? you mentioned <200ms earlier in email?
[01:19] Tom Madsen: yeah we're trying to keep end-to-end lookup + model under 250ms for routing experiences, but segment teams want the model p95 under 120ms to be comfortable. There's some wiggle room if cost delta is huge.
[01:31] Maya Chen: to be explicit: Redwood's suggested acceptance gates — model p95 generation <= 120ms for typical 64-token prompts, end-to-end p95 <= 250ms, error rate < 0.5% (timeouts/500s), sustained throughput >= described baseline (see workload sizing). Cost per 1k tokens should not exceed your guardrail, which you'll provide.
[01:45] Priya Singh: that seems reasonable. We'll set cost guardrail in the doc.
[01:49] Carlos Rivera: on workload sizing, can you confirm traffic profile? average rps and holiday peak?
[01:54] Priya Singh: baseline is 35 rps globally, peak is 220 rps during promotions (5x), average tokens per request is 48 but we have a 10% tail at 200+ tokens.
[02:08] Carlos Rivera: good -- we'll size bench to replay a 220 rps peak burst for a 10-minute window and run a 1-hour sustained at 40 rps for steady-state metrics. We'll also include a mixed prompt distribution to capture the 10% long tail.
[02:22] Evan Park: networking: we'll need to schedule a VPC peering window and add Redwood IPs to allowlist. also, if you want private deployment tests, we need to hash out certs.
[02:32] Maya Chen: for this POC we'll run in dedicated-hosted mode hitting your sample traffic via a secure tunnel; if private/on-prem is necessary later we'll scope it separately.
[02:40] Priya Singh: ok that works. who will run the baseline first?
[02:42] Carlos Rivera: Redwood will run first set once you share the representative sample and whitelist the test IPs. Expect three runs: baseline, quantized, cached. Each run will produce the CSV of per-request latencies and the aggregated metrics sheet.
[02:56] Lina Duarte: what fields will be in the CSV?
[03:00] Carlos Rivera: we'll standardize: timestamp, request_id, prompt_length_tokens, response_length_tokens, model_variant, batch_size, generation_time_ms, end_to_end_time_ms, status_code, semantic_score (embedding cosine), intent_label, predicted_intent. We'll share schema in the template.
[03:18] Priya Singh: please include a column for cache_hit boolean - we want to see the delta with and without prefix caching.
[03:24] Carlos Rivera: yes will do.
[03:26] Maya Chen: about reporting format — recommended is: run-level PDF summary + raw CSV and a pre-populated summary CSV that contains the gating booleans (pass/fail) for each acceptance criteria. we'll also publish a dashboard link in the console with daily refresh during the run window.
[03:42] Tom Madsen: what about frequency - we want an interim snapshot after the peak burst and a final consolidated report.
[03:48] Maya Chen: we'll provide a run summary within 2 hours of completion, and full artifact bundle within 24 hours.
[03:54] Priya Singh: sounds good. any concerns about model selection? we want something cost-effective but accurate — can you compare a 70B-ish open model (quantized) vs a 13B fp16?
[04:05] Carlos Rivera: absolutely — we'll include those two model variants plus a cached variant of the 13B. We'll also show tokenization variance impact. The bench script will log total token consumption to allow cost projection.
[04:18] Lina Duarte: acceptance gating: do we require all gates to be met for a pass? or a weighted pass/fail?
[04:24] Maya Chen: we propose a primary gate set (must pass): intent accuracy and p95 generation latency. Secondary gates (nice-to-have): cost-per-1k, p99 latency, cache hit improvements. If a primary gate fails it's a no-go. We can propose tunings if it's close.
[04:39] Priya Singh: ok that's fair. could you put numeric thresholds in the template?
[04:42] Maya Chen: yes, we'll pre-fill with suggested numbers: intent accuracy >= 92%, generation p95 <= 120ms, end-to-end p95 <= 250ms, error rate < 0.5%. You can edit.
[04:53] Carlos Rivera: small note: for quantized runs we'll also capture any delta in semantic_score and regen rates. quantization can shave cost but sometimes reduces similarity.
[05:01] Tom Madsen: who is the final sign-off from Vertex? Priya is the technical owner but product will sign off?
[05:06] Priya Singh: Priya will sign technical, Lina will sign product acceptance, and Tom will confirm infra constraints.
[05:12] Maya Chen: great - we'll add that to the acceptance doc as the approvers list.
[05:16] Evan Park: on security - SOC2 report and network diagram would be helpful. we expect no PII in the sample traffic but we'll sanitize.
[05:24] Maya Chen: Redwood will share SOC2 summary and redacted network diagrams, plus a short note on retention policy (default 30 days for POC logs).
[05:31] Priya Singh: for audit we need an immutable CSV and a hash fingerprint. can you provide MD5 or SHA logs?
[05:37] Carlos Rivera: yes we can generate checksums for the CSV bundles.
[05:40] Lina Duarte: timeline recap?
[05:42] Maya Chen: agreed timeline: Maya sends template by Oct 9. Vertex provides traffic and approvals by Oct 12. Redwood runs benchmarks week of Oct 19 (we'll pick exact windows during peering). First results call Oct 22. Final acceptance decision within 3 business days after results.
[05:58] Priya Singh: that timing works for us.
[06:02] Maya Chen: any other questions or blockers?
[06:05] Tom Madsen: none from platform. just need the allowlist window.
[06:08] Evan Park: I'll coordinate times - expect an email from me.
[06:10] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll follow up in writing with everything. Thanks all.
[06:15] Priya Singh: thanks everyone. bye.

Recap / explicit acceptance gates (read-back):
- Primary pass gates: intent accuracy >= 92% on labelled set; model p95 generation <= 120ms (for <=64-token prompts); end-to-end p95 <= 250ms; error rate <0.5%
- Secondary gates: p99 latency improvements with caching, cost per 1k tokens stays within Vertex guardrail, semantic similarity >= 0.86
- Reporting: per-request CSV + aggregated metrics CSV + run-level PDF + dashboard link. Checksums included.
